title: Bots find leaked API keys in a minute

beats.say: Push an API key to GitHub, and bots can start using it before you've closed the tab.
In one test, researchers leaked AWS keys on GitHub. Attackers started abusing them within one minute.
GitHub found over thirty nine million leaked secrets in 2024 alone.
AI-built apps leak keys a second way, inside the code your visitors download.
In Vite, any variable that starts with VITE is baked into your public JavaScript. Anyone can open dev tools and copy it.
Then someone else runs their AI on your bill.
Keys belong on a server, never in the browser. And if one leaks, rotate it. Deleting the commit isn't enough.
Here's the prompt. Screenshot it, and send it to Claude inside your project.
Follow Ship With Pip for one of these every day.

prompt: Scan this repo and its full git history for API keys and secrets, including .env files and any VITE_ or NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables that ship to the browser. Move every secret behind a server-side endpoint, add .env to .gitignore, and list exactly which keys I need to rotate.
caption: Leaked keys get used fast: in Comparitech's GitHub honeypot, attackers abused exposed AWS keys within a minute. GitHub detected 39M+ leaked secrets in 2024. Vibe-coded apps add a second leak: Vite exposes any VITE_ variable in the public JS bundle. Keep keys server-side, and if one leaks, rotate it. The prompt is at the end.
sources: Comparitech GitHub honeypot: AWS key abused within 1 minute; >1,000 RunInstances calls within a minute in a later test
Orca 2023 honeypot report: GitHub secrets found <5 min
Vite docs: VITE_-prefixed env vars are exposed to client code
